summary: Frontend-only retest verifying the Google OAuth callback freeze fix. All 6 required checks pass: (1) POST /api/auth/google/session with invalid session returns 401 (not 500 or hang); (2) landing on app with #session_id=<fake> and no token no longer freezes on 'ENTERING THE COURT…'; the frontend calls /auth/google/session, receives 401, hard-redirects to a clean URL (no hash) and renders auth-screen within ~1s; (3) with a valid dsc_token pre-seeded in localStorage and #session_id=<fake> in URL, the callback resolves, redirects to clean URL, AuthContext calls /auth/me (200) and renders cover-screen — no freeze, no auth-screen; (4) email/password regression (farrukh@test.com / vault123) still logs in and reaches cover-screen; (5) 'Continue with Google' button (data-testid auth-google-btn) navigates the browser to https://auth.emergentagent.com (which in turn forwards to Google). No console errors from the app itself observed during the callback flow.
critical_code_review_comments: GoogleCallback catches ALL errors silently (empty catch). If /auth/google/session ever returns 5xx or network error, user is redirected back to login with no feedback. Consider surfacing a toast (e.g., 'Google sign-in failed, please try again') before the hard redirect.

window.location.replace(origin + pathname) works because on real cross-origin returns from Google the navigation is a full document load, so the subsequent replace triggers a reload. If the hash-callback flow were ever entered from the SAME document (same-page hash change), replace() would be a fragment navigation only and would NOT reload React. This is not an issue for the current OAuth flow but is a latent footgun — safer to also call window.location.reload() after replace(), or use window.location.assign / a small guard that forces reload.

AuthContext skips /auth/me whenever window.location.hash includes 'session_id='. If the redirect ever failed to strip the hash, the app would render auth-screen even with a valid token in localStorage. Consider also clearing the hash defensively inside AuthContext (history.replaceState) before deciding.
Regex .replace('#','') in GoogleCallback strips only the first '#'; fine for the current single-hash format, but URLSearchParams(hash.slice(1)) would be clearer/safer.
GoogleCallback loading text 'ENTERING THE COURT…' has no data-testid; adding one (e.g., 'google-callback-loading') would make future regression tests for the freeze bug more robust.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Google OAuth freeze bug (ENTERING THE COURT…) is confirmed FIXED. When simulating the OAuth return, ensure the browser genuinely reloads: navigate first to about:blank (or another origin) then goto BASE + '#session_id=fake'. Setting localStorage token followed by a same-origin goto with only-hash change is a same-document navigation in Playwright and will NOT full-reload React — this initially looked like a bug but was a test artifact. Use page.context.add_init_script to persist the token across the reload triggered by window.location.replace. Endpoints exercised: POST /api/auth/login (200), GET /api/auth/me (200), POST /api/auth/google/session (401 for invalid).
rca of the issue: Original bug: GoogleCallback set isCallback=true on mount and rendered 'ENTERING THE COURT…'; on failure of /auth/google/session it swallowed the error but never navigated away, so the component stayed mounted forever. Fix: after the session exchange (success OR failure), GoogleCallback now calls window.location.replace(origin + pathname) which triggers a full document reload to the clean URL. On reload, Shell sees no #session_id hash → isCallback=false, and AuthContext runs /auth/me — if a token was stored (success path) it shows cover-screen, otherwise it shows auth-screen. Verified end-to-end from a fresh browsing context.
